Background

UNDP is the leading United Nations organization fighting to end the injustice of poverty, inequality, and climate change. Working with our broad network of experts and partners in 170 countries, we help nations to build integrated, lasting solutions for people and planet.

UNDP’s Programme of Assistance to the Palestinian People (PAPP) derives its mandate from United Nations General Assembly Resolution 33/147 of 20 December 1978. Called upon by United Nations Member States in that year, UNDP was requested “to improve the economic and social conditions of the Palestinian people by identifying their social and economic needs and by establishing concrete projects to that end”.

UNDP’s Palestinian Programmatic Framework (PPF) 2023-2027 sets out a vision of “a world in which all Palestinians can enjoy a dignified life and fulfil their own vision of a unified, peaceful and free society”. The PPF is centered around the concept of “Transformative Resilience” and its three elements: a cohesive Palestinian identity, self-reliance, and ownership and leadership.

Over the next three years, UNDP/PAPP will build on its experiences and achievements to make critical contributions to the priorities defined by the Palestinian national development plans and the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF), through interventions in three programmatic priority areas: i) democratic governance and quality services; ii) inclusive economic opportunities; iii) sustainable natural resources management.

The SHAMSI Palestine is a national renewable energy and municipal finance platform established to enable Palestinian Local Government Units (LGUs) to develop, own, and operate solar photovoltaic (PV) and battery energy storage system (BESS) projects through a structured blended financing model combining programme participation and local bank financing. The Project aims to transform LGUs from electricity consumers into active energy investors; reduce municipal electricity expenditure; strengthen financial sustainability; support electricity-sector reform; and contribute to national renewable energy and energy-security targets. SHAMSI is implemented through a programme-coordinated, municipality-implemented delivery model. The Role

The Senior Accounting & Finance Data Analyst is the analytics owner for Tala's accounting and finance reporting function across all markets (PH, KE, MX, GT, PA, VN, DO, IN). This role is responsible for the queries, data logic, and documentation behind monthly close reporting, statutory and tax reporting, and external audit support — work where correctness and traceability are non-negotiable because the outputs feed statutory filings and Big-4 audits.

Unlike a standard product analyst role, accounting and audit domain context is essential. The immediate mandate is to stabilize and fully document a currently under-documented reporting estate, ensure continuity through the 2026 external audit cycle, and help migrate this reporting onto governed, version-controlled infrastructure (Presentation Layer / dbt) while moving the function toward self-serve. The role partners daily with the Controllership/Accounting team and closely with Analytics Engineering.

What You'll Do

Accounting & Audit Reporting Ownership

Own the queries and data logic behind monthly close reporting, tax reporting (VAT, DST, GRT and market equivalents), reserve/provisioning, transaction and cash-rollforward schedules across all markets.
Own delivery of external audit support: loan-level listing details, cash rollforward schedules, subsequent-collections and guarantee asset/liability reports, and ad-hoc auditor requests through the audit cycle.
Ensure every report is traceable end to end — request, query, and final output connected and documented to an audit-ready standard.

Documentation, Governance & Migration

Bring an under-documented estate up to a documentation-first standard: version-controlled queries (Git), clear lineage, and business-logic documentation that does not live in one person's head.
Partner with Analytics Engineering to migrate reporting off legacy infrastructure (Business_DB) onto the Presentation Layer / dbt model with proper testing and version control.
Maintain the accounting master report list as a living single source of truth linking each report to its query and output.

Reconciliation & Domain Rigor

Own reconciliation logic and the "numbers must tie" standard — especially loan-level and cash-rollforward reconciliation, and partner/channeling reconciliation (e.g., Maya loan channeling).
Handle multi-entity, multi-market regulatory variation, including fast-turnaround regulatory reporting (e.g., India RBI, often <3-day SLA).

What You'll Need

4–6 years in data/analytics roles with substantial experience in financial or accounting reporting.
Expert SQL; fluency with Snowflake or equivalent cloud data warehouse; able to read, refactor, and document inherited queries and stored procedures.
Direct experience working with external auditors (Big-4 statutory audits preferred) — familiar with audit cycles, loan-level/reconciliation requests, and the documentation and traceability standard auditors require.
Experience documenting business processes, reporting logic, and functional requirements to create repeatable, maintainable solutions.
Mindset focused on standardization, scalability, and continuous process improvement, with an eye toward reducing manual work and increasing the reliability of Finance operations.
Experience producing month-end close, tax, and regulatory reporting, ideally across multiple markets/entities.
Intermediate Python

The Role

The Senior Accounting & Finance Data Analyst is the analytics owner for Tala's accounting and finance reporting function across all markets (PH, KE, MX, GT, PA, VN, DO, IN). This role is responsible for the queries, data logic, and documentation behind monthly close reporting, statutory and tax reporting, and external audit support — work where correctness and traceability are non-negotiable because the outputs feed statutory filings and Big-4 audits.

Unlike a standard product analyst role, accounting and audit domain context is essential. The immediate mandate is to stabilize and fully document a currently under-documented reporting estate, ensure continuity through the 2026 external audit cycle, and help migrate this reporting onto governed, version-controlled infrastructure (Presentation Layer / dbt) while moving the function toward self-serve. The role partners daily with the Controllership/Accounting team and closely with Analytics Engineering.

What You'll Do

Accounting & Audit Reporting Ownership

Own the queries and data logic behind monthly close reporting, tax reporting (VAT, DST, GRT and market equivalents), reserve/provisioning, transaction and cash-rollforward schedules across all markets.
Own delivery of external audit support: loan-level listing details, cash rollforward schedules, subsequent-collections and guarantee asset/liability reports, and ad-hoc auditor requests through the audit cycle.
Ensure every report is traceable end to end — request, query, and final output connected and documented to an audit-ready standard.

Documentation, Governance & Migration

Bring an under-documented estate up to a documentation-first standard: version-controlled queries (Git), clear lineage, and business-logic documentation that does not live in one person's head.
Partner with Analytics Engineering to migrate reporting off legacy infrastructure (Business_DB) onto the Presentation Layer / dbt model with proper testing and version control.
Maintain the accounting master report list as a living single source of truth linking each report to its query and output.

Reconciliation & Domain Rigor

Own reconciliation logic and the "numbers must tie" standard — especially loan-level and cash-rollforward reconciliation, and partner/channeling reconciliation (e.g., Maya loan channeling).
Handle multi-entity, multi-market regulatory variation, including fast-turnaround regulatory reporting (e.g., India RBI, often <3-day SLA).

Expert SQL; fluency with Snowflake or equivalent cloud data warehouse; able to read, refactor, and document inherited queries and stored procedures.
Direct experience working with external auditors (Big-4 statutory audits preferred) — familiar with audit cycles, loan-level/reconciliation requests, and the documentation and traceability standard auditors require.
Experience documenting business processes, reporting logic, and functional requirements to create repeatable, maintainable solutions.
Mindset focused on standardization, scalability, and continuous process improvement, with an eye toward reducing manual work and increasing the reliability of Finance operations.
Experience producing month-end close, tax, and regulatory reporting, ideally across multiple markets/entities.

Position Title

About the Organization
: Kōkua Hawaiʻi Foundation is a 501(c)3 non-profit organization founded in 2003 that supports environmental education in the schools and communities of Hawaiʻi. We provide opportunities that enhance appreciation for and understanding of the environment to inspire lifelong stewards of the earth. In 2019 KHF acquired 8 acres of land in Haleʻiwa to establish agricultural, educational, and retail activities that benefit the community and promote local food, waste reduction, and environmental stewardship. 

Position Description
: Kōkua Hawaiʻi Foundation (KHF) operates a range of environmental education programs. Program Coordinators help to support, strengthen, and grow KHF programs in their area of experience and interest. Programs include: the 3Rs School Program,
Plastic Free Hawaiʻi
, ʻĀINA In Schools,
Kōkua Learning Farm Youth Internship Program
, Kōkua Learning Farm Field Trips, Kōkua Compost Program
. The ideal candidate has experience with hands-on waste reduction and ʻāina-based education. They also have experience working with various communities throughout Hawaiʻi, including school administration, faculty, students, community groups, and volunteers.

Roles and Responsibilities: 

General Support for KHF Programs

Collaborate with KHF program staff and school education teams in planning and implementing programs and trainings at participating schools throughout Oʻahu and on the Kōkua Learning Farm in Haleʻiwa.
Develop and maintain relationships and communication with school administrators, teachers, students, and partner organizations, including understanding the diverse needs of the communities they serve, in order to successfully deliver programs.
Lead and assist with program events, including planning, delivery, supplies, and other logistics. Program events may include recycling drives, beach cleanups, waste reduction service events, school presentations, classroom visits, community outreach events, and educator trainings at partner schools and sites throughout Oʻahu and on the Kōkua Learning Farm in Haleʻiwa.
Procure, distribute, and track inventory of program supplies. 
Provide photos, video, written content, and participant testimonials from program events and outreach events for newsletters, social media and in-house reports.

Specialized Support for KHF Programs –
KHF assigns
additional program support responsibilities in the areas of Food, Waste, and/or Place, based on employee experience and expertise. The ideal candidate for this position brings extensive experience in waste reduction systems and practices to support the following program areas:

3Rs School Program - empowers students to engage and educate their school community about the 3Rs of waste reduction,
Lead coordination and implementation of educational trainings/presentations and distribute educational materials to schools participating in the 3R’s School Program. 
Assist Oʻahu schools with implementation of student-led on-campus recycling systems.
Coordinate and promote 3R’s Recycling Drives at Oʻahu DOE schools with recycling partners, school administration, teachers, students, and community groups.

Provide on-site logistical support, coordination, and direction at all 3R’s Program Events.

Plastic Free Hawaiʻi - provides resources, tools, and trainings to educate about the environmental and health benefits of going plastic free to minimize single-use plastics in our islands
Lead coordination and promotion of beach cleanups with partners, schools, businesses, and/or community groups, including coordination of permits and refuse pickup/drop off.
Lead the annual Plastic Free Hawaiʻi School Mural Contest, including creation of promotional materials, contest logistics and communications, and coordination of the PFH School Mural Art Show.
Manage the Plastic Free Hawaiʻi Water Refill Stations. This includes:
Transporting water stations to various community events around Oʻahu
Setting up and breaking down water stations at community events.
Tracking and guiding the use of the Plastic Free Hawai’i Water Refill Stations for schools, community groups, and partner organizations.
Maintaining and repairing the water stations as needed.
Identify opportunities, promote and support composting, cafeteria waste audits, campus waste audits, and waste reduction campaigns in schools, community events and businesses
Kōkua Compost Program - engages keiki & community in hands-on learning about the importance of turning food scraps into compost
Assist with developing and delivering education materials and curriculum related to composting using various composting systems, from backyard vermicast (worm) systems, to an in-vessel industrial scale compost machine.
Support weekly collection of food scraps, data collection, monitoring, cleaning, and maintenance for various composting systems. 
 Farm Education

KLF Field Trips - engages students with an enriching farm experience while allowing them to explore various aspects of agriculture
Lead school-aged students and their teachers and chaperones in hands-on farm-based learning.
Integrate KHF educational programs and resources related to food, waste, and place, as appropriate to the school and age group.

KLF Youth Internship - provides on-farm training to build skills around agroecology, food production, culinary explorations, soil health, and composting,
Support teens in growing and cooking healthy local food, promoting soil health, connecting to place, and engaging in service learning activities throughout the Kōkua Learning Farm.

ʻĀINA In Schools - a farm to school initiative connecting children to their local land, waters, and food to grow a healthier Hawaiʻi,
Support ʻĀINA In Schools education teams (faculty, staff, parents, volunteers) with program needs and assist with continued integration of all ʻĀINA In Schools components, including the Waste Reduction component.

Data Tracking, Networking, and Administration

Maintain accurate, up-to-date digital systems for planning program operations, tracking program impact, and managing team tasks.
Track and report on program inputs, outputs, and outcomes in a timely and accurate manner.

Assist with developing and implementing evaluation tools. 
Represent KHF at conferences, meetings, and other events. 

Assist with other KHF-related tasks as needed.
Seek and participate in professional development opportunities.

The ideal candidate meets most of these qualifications and is willing and able to develop further skills through on-the-job training and mentorship.

Demonstrated knowledge of and experience with practicing and teaching at least one of the following program areas:
The 3Rs, reducing single-use plastic & plastic pollution, and promoting waste reduction processes and practices
Composting organic waste to reduce waste and promote soil health
ʻĀina-based education and garden-based learning
Willingness to be flexible and adaptable in workflow, schedule, and communications
Experience working with children and teachers in a school or outdoor setting 
Experience developing and formatting educational curricula, lesson plans, and materials 
Strong interpersonal and communication skills and the ability to work effectively with a wide range of constituencies in diverse communities  
Strong written language skills, including the ability to create, compose, and edit written materials 
Excellent speaking and presentation skills 
Experience working with, organizing, and leading volunteers 
Highly organized, tidy, and detail oriented 
First Aid trained, or willingness to be trained
Beginning level proficiency in ʻŌlelo Hawaiʻi or interest and commitment to learning
Commitment to sustainability, intersectional environmentalism, and growing a healthier future for Hawaiʻi 
Proactive and able to work independently and in a collaborative work environment 
Able to lift up to 50+ pounds and work outdoors for extended periods of time for recycling drives, beach cleanups, water station installation, trainings, and in-vessel compost machine maintenance 
Strong Apple computer skills and proficiency in Google Suite (Drive, Calendars, Docs, Sheets, Slides), and the ability to learn to use new programs and databases as needed. 
Proficiency in Canva
Able to work on Saturdays and some evenings 
Has their own mobile phone and willingness to use it for communications with KHF, schools, and volunteers (communication reimbursement provided)
Has regular access to a personal vehicle for frequent school visits and meetings/events at multiple locations around Oʻahu (mileage reimbursement provided)
3 years Hawaiʻi-based work experience and 3 Hawaiʻi-based professional references
BA/BS degree or higher, in a related field, or commensurate skills through experience

Full-time and part-time positions are available, and the work week includes most Saturdays and some evenings. The ideal candidate must be available to work Tuesday-Saturday. Email cover letter and resume with three references to jobs@kokuahawaiifoundation.org. We are looking for someone to start for the 2026-27 academic year. Applications will be accepted until the position is filled, please apply ASAP.

a plan for their future and a mentor whose impact will last a lifetime. We are a dynamic, mission-driven team of professionals who are empowered, engaged, and ambitious. We
work collaboratively and boldly, never afraid to challenge the status quo if it means a better future for Idaho’s youth. 

The Opportunity

We are seeking a Program Coordinator/Match Support Specialist to support the
volunteers, children, and families enrolled in our program. Match Support is the “Secret Sauce” of our organization’s success. In this role, you will work directly with participants to ensure child safety, foster positive youth development, and maintain high standards of relationship sustainability.
You are the right fit if you are an independent thinker, a self-starter, and someone who is energized by people. You are a mindful listener who can remain calm and professional during difficult or emotionally charged interactions, and you aren't afraid to navigate challenging coaching conversations. Beyond core caseload management, you will also have the opportunity to lead a special project: managing our brand-new High School Bigs program (launching fall 2027). 

What You'll Do

Stellar Caseload Management:
Serve as the primary bridge between the BBBS mission and match participants. Complete consistent, interactive monthly/quarterly outreach (via phone, text, email, and in-person) to meet or exceed agency and national standards.
Relationship Coaching & Support:
Provide ongoing coaching, training, and solution-focused resources to volunteer Bigs, Littles, and parents/guardians to sustain long-lasting relationships.
Child Safety & Assessment:
Continuously assess match health and document relationships with a strict focus on child safety. Identify potential threats to a child's well-being both within and outside the match, delivering necessary and strategic interventions.
Data & Compliance Excellence:
Maintain accurate, up-to-date, and detailed documentation within Matchforce (our federation database). Utilize data to track outcomes , fulfill grant requirements/MOUs , and facilitate the match closure and re-match process when necessary.
Meet & Greets:
Conduct intentional, in-person match introductions between families and volunteers to spark early relationship development and ensure a smooth transition from enrollment to active support. 
Specialty Program Coordination:
Support the strategic planning, launch, and ongoing implementation of the High School Bigs program, alongside managing site-based programming at assigned locations.
Community Integration:
Collect impactful photos and stories from the field to champion the agency's broader efforts. 

What You Bring

Mission & Values Alignment:
A deep commitment to living out BBBS Core Values. Dedicated to working inclusively with diverse populations and cultures.
Experience:
A Bachelor’s degree or 4+ years of relevant work experience is required (Human Services or Youth Development backgrounds preferred). Experience with intake, interviewing, or child/adult behavioral assessment is a major plus. Communication Skills:
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills; someone who is highly comfortable on the phone and writes in a clear, concise, and professional manner.
Execution & Tech Savvy:
Strong attention to detail, time management, and the ability to multitask in a fast-paced environment. Proficient with Microsoft Suite
and database experience (especially Salesforce/Matchforce) is a significant advantage.
Growth Mindset:
Coachable, eager to grasp new skills quickly, and committed to participating in 20 hours of professional development annually.
Logistics:
A valid Idaho driver’s license, a good driving record, and access to a reliable, fully insured vehicle. Must successfully pass a comprehensive background screening (including fingerprinting and a Motor Vehicle check). 

What's in it for You

We believe taking care of our team is just as important as taking care of our mission. Your total compensation includes a salary range beginning at $40,000 (DOE) plus a comprehensive benefits package valued at an additional $5,000-$8,000:
100% Company-Paid Health Coverage:
Medical, dental, and vision insurance at zero cost to you.
Retirement Security:
A SIMPLE IRA with a company match to invest in your future.
Student Loan Forgiveness:
We are a qualifying employer under the Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) program.
• True Work-Life Integration:
Generous PTO, flexible daily scheduling, work from
home opportunities, and a casual "dress for your day" culture.
Extra Time to Unplug:
In addition to federal holidays, we feature two annual paid week-long holiday shutdowns so the entire team can rest.

To Apply

Please send your resume and a cover letter detailing why you are the perfect fit for this role to Kris at kbryant@bbbsidaho.org.
